idea-plugin.name: Piwi
idea-plugin.description:
Your Playwright suite's history in the IDE, from a Piwi instance:
  • the failures of the latest CI run on the checked-out branch, as your local runs since leave them, at their failing lines, with the recommended locator heal as a quick fix, the trace and the screenshot one action away;
  • the Piwi tool window: the latest run's failures as a tree, grouped by file, cluster or owner, with the runs you made since, compared with the branch's latest run, another branch's, a run by its id or your local runs only, and each test re-run, its trace and screenshot one right-click away; a run started from Piwi pauses at your breakpoints in the browser, where a locator you pick replaces the one on that line;
  • each test's latest result in the gutter, a failing test's body tinted, and the tests behind each locator line and each application file;
  • with coverage recorded, the lines your tests ran, in TypeScript, JavaScript and C# alike: marks in the gutter, the tests behind each function and line, and the lines changed since the coverage run;
  • brittle locators, and the locators an unsaved change breaks, with quick fixes;
  • the latest run in the status bar, with the run you started as it runs, its tests in the gutter as they end, and what it changed once it ended; read again on a click; and Piwi's MCP server for your AI assistant;
  • tests recorded in a browser your project's own Playwright opens, written at the caret as you click and type, with calls to your page objects and helpers when connected, and removed in one undo;
  • locators and recorded flows sent from the Piwi Picker browser extension, inserted at the caret;
  • the source paths clicked in the dashboard, opened at their line in the project that holds them.
It reads the connection the Piwi reporter uses (the environment, the workspace .env, the Piwi desktop app); otherwise connect under Settings → Tools → Piwi, signing in with the browser. The Piwi desktop app sits beside a shared instance: Connect switches between them, keeping both. Works in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate, Rider and the other IDEs with the LSP API and JavaScript support.
